type_why: The Spark catches her surface. She is up at 4:30, cannot bear a quiet room and fills it with stories. But half the type is written for someone young: "You start more than you finish", a trap about drink and lust, and Augustine before his conversion as her kindred. It is also word for word the type Marcus got, so none of the headline is hers. It misses her centre. She is a giver who needs to be needed, and she keeps count. Her own answers held that pattern: "Ask for my help", "Of course. I'll sort out my own needs later", "I want people to notice my good work", "I care what people think of me", and Vainglory at 66. The report never joins them up. Self-report hides the scorekeeping, since she believes she never keeps score. Still, the questions gave enough to name it.

links.link: You said you let rudeness go. You also said hours later
links.why: This is her quiet hurt, the "It's okay, anak" that is not okay. The list of people who never thanked her lives in her head for years. Hers is resentment more than wishing she had been harsher, but it is close. It contradicts the report's own anger section, which says her anger does not last.

links.link: You said you let things slide that you probably should not
links.why: She spoils her son and complains about him to everyone except him. She is putting off asking her nephew for the 30,000 pesos. "Keeping the peace can be love. It can also be the easier road" fits both.

links.link: You said you are nothing but glad when friends succeed
links.why: Nothing in her life suggests she cheers from the stands without acting. She is the most active person in any room. It is a stock line set off by one answer pair.

links.link: You said your mood is usually light. You also said after a hard day
links.why: It repeats the type's lust quote a second time, aimed at a devout widow of 67. Her "treat" is a snack. Nothing in her life or her friend's view points to pleasure-seeking as her pull.

fight_should_be: Vainglory, which scored 66 in her own list. She gives and then mentions it for ten years. She notices who does not thank her. She needs to be needed and even organised the hospital ward. Nothing in her life points to food. Gluttony won because the forced pairs set food against flirting and a snack against boredom. A devout widow of 67 will pick food every time without it meaning anything. The fight scoring should not let the least-bad option of a forced pair win.
line_why: The Host fits exactly: pancit sent to a wake, a house that feeds everyone. The Watcher as second fits the rosary on the jeepney. The Macarius line checks out word for word against Cassian (Conferences XIV.4).
leanings_wrong: When wronged: Lets it go (83). True only in the moment. Her friend and her own story show a list of slights kept for years. Her answers hinted at it ("Hours later, I think of what I should have said", "One raised eyebrow can stay with me all day").

Candour: Says it plainly (33). When hurt she goes quiet and serves food with great politeness. She complains about her son to everyone except him. She chooses what to show. This is her self-image, not what her friend sees.
wording_issues: "The pull you are least guarded against is the pull of a good time.  Counsel:" A double space where a quotation is missing.
"Gregory says this is the one closest to peace of mind.  One caution from Chrysostom" Another missing quotation.

"One caution from Chrysostom: calm that is never tested is not yet patience. Stay among people." This caution is meant for recluses. Telling a woman who organised a hospital ward from her bed to "stay among people" makes no sense.
"For because pleasure borders on mirth, he holds out lust as a bait to cheerful dispositions." The "he" is the devil, who is never named, so a reader may take it to mean God.
"He was just as honest, later, about where his love of pleasure had led him." Just as honest as what? A comma stack.
"What feeds it: It comes first on Cassian's list, and it opens the door to the others." It does not answer the question its own label asks.
"Fluent, not deep." She already calls herself "not very clever", so this reads as a put-down that confirms it.
"All eight: Gluttony 100, Vainglory 66, Pride 63..." A score out of 100 against each sin reads like a percentage against the person.
best_moment: "Gregory warns the generous against giving so much at once that they run short and start grumbling." This is her nephew's 30,000 pesos and her own blood-pressure medicine. The counsel that follows, "do not keep score", is exactly what Tessie says about her.
worst_moment: "One more drink, one more episode, one more look than you meant to give." This lust-bait line goes to a devout 67-year-old widow and is repeated in a later section. Nothing in her life supports it, and it could read as insulting.

type_why: His three strongest leanings are all anger (Lets them know 0, Fiery 0, Takes a stand 0), yet the type is the cheerful Spark, word for word what Lola got. "Your mood is light" and "a full one makes you happy" miss the man who goes silent for days, and his own answers said so ("I go quiet and heavy", "Everything feels heavy"). "One more drink" lands by luck, but it frames the cans as fun when he drinks to wind down. The report's biggest miss had data behind it. He answered "I don't always notice I've upset someone until they tell me" at the strongest setting. Put next to Fiery 0, that is Dean's "no idea how frightening he is" and Ellie's question, and the report never says it. Self-report cannot be blamed for missing the drinking as a problem. He denies it, and the questions only ask about "something to eat or drink".

links.link: You said you let people know on the spot
links.why: He is shouting before he knows he has started, then feels shame when he catches Ellie's eyes in the mirror. "The care arrives too late" is exactly him.

links.link: You said you tell people in charge when they are wrong
links.why: It meets his self-image head on. He thinks he is "honest and straightforward", and he blames his ex for everything. "The feeling of being right is not proof" is the thing Dean would want him to hear.

links.link: You said your mood is usually light. You also said after a hard day
links.why: This is a copy of Lola's link. His "treat" is four or five cans until noon. The link aims at pleasure and lust instead of numbing, and it ignores the heaviness his own answers showed.

links.link: You said you fix things and move on
links.why: This is the strongest line in his report. It is the can from the machine and "no hard feelings, yeah?" as if that settles it. It is fixing your car instead of saying sorry. The debtor image fits a man who thinks it is over in a minute.

fight_should_be: Anger, which scored 68 and came third. Ellie's question and Dean's "eggshells" make it the live fight right now. Gluttony, at 87, is a close second: its own text ("Reaching for food or drink to take the edge off") is exactly his cans. Either beats Pride. Pride's "How it shows" ("Thinking every serious talk is aimed at you") is not him, and its "How it talks to you" quotation is missing. The fight scoring ignored his most extreme leanings.
line_why: The Advocate is his own pick twice and fits his loyalty, since he would square up to anyone for his mates. But it comes with no word of the warning the report gives elsewhere, that temper can dress as zeal, so it feeds his "raw deal" story. "Your gladness is a gift" is the stock Spark line and misses his real gift, which is his big heart. He knows whose mum is poorly and covers breaks unasked. That is closer to the Caregiver or the Shepherd.
help_card_wrong: "Say it straight. I can take it." He also answered "I find it hard to take correction, even when it's fair", and the report's own Pride section uses that answer. Dean says people walk on eggshells round him.
"Point out everything. I would rather know." This is the same contradiction. A full list of faults is the likeliest thing to set off the fuse.
leanings_wrong: Mood: Light-hearted (25). He goes silent for days, ignores messages and drinks to wind down. His own answers said "I go quiet and heavy".

Seen and unseen: Better in private (75). He is at his best on shift, where he knows every lad's name. The worst of him lands at home: Ellie walks on eggshells, and he blames his ex. This is his self-image, and Dean sees the opposite.
Correction: Say it straight (0). This contradicts his own answer that correction is hard to take even when fair.
wording_issues: "Gregory says many quarrels grow from pride in a gift that sets us apart, like knowing more or trying harder.  Counsel:" A double space where a quotation is missing.
"Every other fault spoils one virtue. Pride spoils them all.  How it shows:" The "How it talks to you" quotation is missing.
"Pride. Last on Cassian's list, and first in its roots." Cryptic.
"Gregory would call that a pair." Unclear what a "pair" means here.
"Balanced: Little things, Others' wins, Follow-through". The leanings list just above labels two of these "Simply glad (33/100)" and "Hard to finish (67/100)".
"For because pleasure borders on mirth, he holds out lust as a bait" The "he" is never named.
best_moment: "Stopping is good. But Gregory says it does not undo what was done, any more than a debtor clears a debt by borrowing no more. Something still needs saying." This is the can from the machine and "no hard feelings, yeah?", and it is the answer to Ellie's question.
worst_moment: "You rarely hold a grudge." This hands his own excuse back to him ("it's over in a minute, never holds a grudge"). Dean says he blames his ex for everything. His own answer that something someone did to him keeps him awake at 3 a.m. pointed the other way too.

type_why: Mostly right. He is slow and quiet and waits to be sure, and the moment passes: the bathroom has been "next spring" for six springs. Two things misread him. First, "you would rather keep the peace than win" is wrong. He keeps the peace AND wins by quietly going his own way ("as reliable as a wall and just as hard to move"). Link 2 later half-corrects this. Second, the trap is framed as social fear ("What if they are upset?... What if I say it, and it costs me?"). He does not much mind what people think. His fear is of want and of what could go wrong. Gregory Nazianzen as kindred is a loose but fair fit. Arsenius sailing in silence suits his walks alone in the Tatras. Missed with data in hand: he is generous in secret and stingy in public. He picked "Quietly pay for something they can't afford" AND "I keep a little back, just in case". That is Beata's main line about him, and the report never sets the two side by side.

links.link: You said your gut says "let me think" when a friend asks for money
links.why: "It is not greed for more. It is fear of less." This speaks straight to his dilemma: the emergency savings against his youngest's studies in the Netherlands.

links.link: You said you listen more than you talk. You also said you have whole conversations
links.why: This is the aha for a man who "believes he is open to other views; he simply finds most of them wrong". It explains why he never changes his mind: he wins every argument, silently.

links.link: You said you let rudeness go. You also said hours later
links.why: Word for word what Lola got. Nothing in his life shows him wishing he had been harsher. He leaves the room and carries on his way.

links.link: You said you hold back after a hard day. You also said you notice
links.why: He cannot understand why his children pay for three streaming services. Beata fights him for every zloty spent on anything enjoyable. "Judging the undisciplined is where it turns" lands.

line_why: The Teacher is his own pick and fits an engineer who needs the reasons. But Beata's view points to the Giver: secret money to his daughter, 4 a.m. airport runs, fixing things. The report puts that second and never sets it against his greed fight or his thrift counterfeit. That tension was the real aha. The Christ line about fear growing into love fits reasonably.
help_card_wrong: "Argue it out with me. Win fairly and I will come round." Beata says he is as hard to move as a wall. He leaves the room rather than argue, and the report's own link 2 says he wins every argument in his head. This is his self-image, and a friend would laugh at it.
leanings_wrong: Mood: Heavy-hearted (71). He is serious and reserved, not sad. He has quiet pleasures in the allotment, the shed and the Tatras. This label feeds the harsh "heart with no joy inside" line.
Temper: Fiery (33). He leaves the room rather than raise his voice. The same report also lists Temper under "Balanced".
Disagreements: Keeps the peace (75). He avoids the argument but never yields. Read alone, the label suggests he gives way.
wording_issues: "Gregory says people who never begin are usually busy with something else they love. That has to be seen for what it is first.  Counsel:" A vague "That" and a missing quotation.
"Balanced: Others' wins, Temper". The list above labels Temper "Fiery (33/100)".
"Kindred: St Gregory the Theologian: ... | Jeremiah: ... | Abba Arsenius:" Three kindred run into one line with pipes.
"Because the timid dread punishments, he threatens terrors to the fearful." The "he" (the devil) is never named.
"Cassian says cut the desire, not only the spending." An odd line for a man who hardly spends.
"What feeds it: Gregory says sadness runs down into it: a heart with no joy inside looks for comfort in owning things." Two colons in one sentence, and the claim is harsh.
best_moment: "And an argument nobody can answer is easy to win." This is the man who thinks he is open to other views and simply finds most of them wrong.
worst_moment: "a heart with no joy inside looks for comfort in owning things." This is harsh and untrue of a man who buys almost nothing for himself and loves his allotment and the mountains. The report itself had just said his grasping is fear, not greed.

type_why: The Herald fits both how she sees herself and how her friend sees her: first to volunteer, persuasive in a room, confident. The close call it names, The Spark ('always starting something'), fits the four notebooks and forty chairs just as well. 'You can promise more than you can keep' reaches her friend Chioma's 'slightly let-down partners'. The report misses Chioma's central point, that she is scared of stillness, and that is not only a limit of self-report. She answered k3 at full strength ('when I have nothing to do my thoughts get worse, I'm better off busy'), and 'a week at home would wear me out' strongly too. No sentence joins those answers to her busyness. The Restlessness counterfeit comes closest.

links.link: You said you tell people in charge when they are wrong
links.why: This makes the same point as the 'Takes up room' bullet above it, with a second quote. The paragraph is also word for word what p05 got. It is partly true (she sighs at slow people and hates being told what to do), but it is not her main pattern.

links.link: You said you let people know on the spot
links.why: It fits how sharp she is with slow people, sighing out loud. 'The care arrives too late' is a good line.

links.link: You said your mood is usually light
links.why: The quote puts lust in front of a woman whose own answers pointed away from it (food over flirting, praise over attention; lust scored 23). The 'treat yourself' answer behind it was her weakest (-1), and she sleeps five hours and works at midnight. Pleasure is not her pull. Stillness is what she runs from. The text is also identical to p06's.

links.link: You said a friend's success stings a little
links.why: The reframe ('the sting is a compliment you have not said out loud') is nice and plausible for a competitive founder. Nothing in her life or her friend's account centres on envy, though, so it lands as a pleasant aside.

fight_should_be: Listlessness (acedia), her second at 72. Cassian's acedia is the restless kind: it cannot bear the cell, sends a person off to visit and help others as 'a real work of piety', and hates the dull middle of the work. That is Adaeze almost exactly. She fills every evening, helps everybody so nobody gets close, feels 'itchy' in the middle of projects, and gets up and cleans when she is alone. The acedia text the report gave Jake fits her better than it fits him. Pride can be defended (she hates being told what to do and finds correction hard). But the listed sign 'Thinking every serious talk is aimed at you' does not fit her at all. She is the one who does not notice she has upset someone.
line_why: The Teacher fits the free mentoring of secondary-school girls. The Giver as her second fits sending fifty thousand naira to a stranger's hospital bill.
best_moment: Counterfeit: Restlessness. Not being able to stop can feel like faithfulness.
worst_moment: "Fluent, not deep." It is a harsh label for someone that both she and her friend see as brilliant and convincing. Her friend's complaint is about finishing and closeness, not shallowness. It will sting without teaching her anything.
leanings_wrong: Comforts: Enjoys comforts (25/100). This rests weakly on one slight answer. The woman who sleeps five hours and does 'just one more thing' at midnight is not ruled by comfort, and the leaning then drives the misplaced pleasure-and-lust link.

Seen and unseen: balanced (42/100). She answered clearly that people she has just met get the best of her. That is her friend's point that nobody can get close, and blending it into 'balanced' buried the one answer that could have caught it.
help_card_wrong: "Say it straight. I can take it." Her answers say correction is hard to take even when fair, and she hates being told what to do. The report's own Pride section names 'finding correction hard to take' as her sign, so the card contradicts the report.
wording_issues: "Diligence: You keep working when others stop." This contradicts 'Hard to finish (92/100)' and 'You start well, then fade.'
"Strongest leanings: Speaks up, Hard to finish, Takes up room" / "* Takes up room: You speak up to people in charge." The label does not match its gloss, and 'Takes up room' reads as a jab.
"What it costs you: ... Praise can steer you." This repeats the line just above it: 'Whoever praises you can steer you.'
"Gregory would call that a pair." This is vague.
"Right now: Pride. Last on Cassian's list, and first in its roots." This is unclear.
"What feeds it: Cassian says vainglory feeds it. What takes its place: Cassian says its place is taken by humility, built on kindness and a simple heart." The frame is repetitive and clunky.
"And idle talk slides, step by step, into talk about other people." This warns about gossip with nothing in her answers to support it.
"Your line: The Teacher (teaching)." The parenthesis is redundant.

"(They picked: gladly do: Explain something until they finally understand it. / Quietly pay for something they can't afford.; people come for: ...)" This reads like debug output: third person in a second-person report, with '.;' punctuation.

type_why: The Deep Well suits a grave, silent, heavy woman. 'Hurts go deep and stay there' and 'Joy can feel suspicious' ('cheerful people simply haven't lived yet') are accurate. The trap line and 'bitterness that calls itself honesty' reach past her self-view ('not harsh, only honest') to what her sister sees. What it misses: her loneliness, her refusal of help, and the cruelty to Maria 'without meaning to be'. Her grief and her anger with God are beyond self-report. The cruelty was not: she answered 'I don't always notice I've upset someone until they tell me' (-2) and 'I'm not one for saying sorry' (-3), and the report used neither. It also treats her heaviness purely as temperament. For a mother two years after her son's death, that framing risks feeling like a scolding for grief.

links.link: You said you hold back after a hard day
links.why: A strict faster who criticises the lentils fits it. But this is the third time 'the pride of abstinence' appears (the leaning bullet, this link, the counterfeit), so it lands as repetition.

links.link: You said you listen more than you talk
links.why: This is the strongest link. 'An argument nobody can answer is easy to win. It can leave you quietly judging people who never got to reply' fits a woman who keeps count of who came to the memorials and says little.

links.link: You said you tell people in charge when they are wrong
links.why: It is word for word p04's paragraph. It fits loosely (stubborn with doctors) but tells her nothing new.

links.link: You said things stay with you for a while
links.why: It fits the grudges and the memorial count, and heaviness sliding into anger. It reuses the 'cup of discord' quote already used in the trap section.

fight_should_be: Sadness (90) is the live one. Cassian says it follows a loss or anger and makes a person rough with 'those who are near and dear to us'. The report's own sadness text ('The people you love come round, and everything they say seems badly timed') is nearly a portrait of her with Maria. Pride is defensible from her sister's 'always proud and hard' and her refusal of help. But the listed signs ('Thinking every serious talk is aimed at you') are generic, and they never name refusing help, which is where her pride actually shows.
line_why: The Watcher fits exactly: the prayer rope in the dark, the lamp before the icons and at the grave. The Cassian line (Elijah, Elisha, Antony) is real and apt.
best_moment: Watch for bitterness that calls itself honesty.
worst_moment: "Look for joy on purpose." To a mother two years after her son's death, this reads as a scold. The line before it ('a heart with no joy inside goes looking for comfort in owning things') is also wrong about her: she sends back twice as much in eggs and oil.
leanings_wrong: After a mistake: Moves on (83/100). This gives a healthy name to her full-strength 'I stop doing it, but I'm not one for saying sorry', which is exactly her sister's complaint.

Temper: Fiery (8/100) sits beside 'Hard wood. It takes a lot to make you angry', which contradicts it on the same page. 'It just burns where no one can see it' is also untrue: Maria sees it every visit.
Make-up: balanced (58/100). She sits in the doorway for long stretches and finds people wearing. She is plainly a quiet mind, and the mixed reading produced a misleading close call to The Forge.
help_card_wrong: "Give me a push. I am slow to get going." It sits on the same card as "Do not push. I come round in my own time." They mean different things (motivation and persuasion), but they read as a flat contradiction.

"Say it straight. I can take it." This contradicts her answer that correction is hard to take even when fair, and the report's own Pride section. It also sits awkwardly beside "Say 'next time, try this', not 'you did this wrong'."
wording_issues: "He opens his Dialogues alone in a place he says suited "a sad and melancholy disposition", and he wrote that he loved the quiet life and had the busy one forced on him." A long, comma-joined sentence.
"the pride of abstinence" is quoted three times in one report.
"People come to you when something really matters, because you will not treat it lightly." This is generic, and false of an isolated widow who lets no one near.
"Gregory says stubbornness often passes for constancy, and grows from thinking a little too much of our own judgment.  Counsel:" A double space, and no quotation where every other bullet has one.
"Melancholy also runs down into avarice". This is a real Gregory line, but it is applied to a woman whose generosity is the opposite.
"Your strength: Counsel. Its partner: Courage. ... The risk is that you never get round to doing it." It is identical to p06's, and weak for a woman who walks to the grave daily in the August heat.

"(They picked: gladly do: Pray for them every day, without telling them. / Have them over and cook them a meal.; people come for: ...)" This reads like debug output: third person, with '.;' punctuation.

type_why: The Hearth catches the warmth everyone sees ('the nicest guy she knows'). 'Warm, steady, and glad to be where you are' and 'You do not go looking for trouble, and it rarely finds you' are his self-image ('chill... it will all work itself out'), not the truth his friend Kayla sees. This is not a limit of self-report: his own answers held the anxiety. The report lists Nerve as Careful at 79. He answered 'What if I can't?', money keeping him awake at 3am, a criticism staying with him, a raised eyebrow staying all day, and 'I put off the thing that matters most' at full strength (-3), which is the major he has not chosen. The report never pairs these to say that his putting-off is fear, not ease. St Antony as his only kindred is an odd match. Antony's cheer came from twenty years of staying put, the opposite of Jake's nine-day pattern, so it reads as flattery rather than a mirror.

links.link: You said you let rudeness go
links.why: It is plausible, but Jake's problem is not stored-up insults. It is never saying what he thinks. 'Wishing you had been harsher' does not fit a young man who does not seem to hold grudges.

links.link: You said you let things slide that you probably should not
links.why: 'Keeping the peace can be love. It can also be the easier road.' That is his 'haha yeah' texts exactly.

links.link: You said your mood is usually light
links.why: The template is shared word for word with p04. The outcome fits (one more episode at 4am), but the mechanism is wrong. His pleasure sits next to dread, not next to cheerfulness. He games so he does not have to think.

links.link: You said you let small things slide
links.why: It fits the few minutes late every shift, the nine-day routines, and the loans adding up. 'No drop matters until the river floods' lands.

line_why: The Caregiver matches his kindness to his half-sister and his patience with old customers, and he picked it twice. But 'You sit with people, and you do not leave' overclaims for someone whose pattern is to quietly drop things and escape into games when life gets hard.
best_moment: Gregory says the changeable do not trust their own judgment, because they think too little of themselves.
worst_moment: "You do not go looking for trouble, and it rarely finds you." His own answers showed the stress his friend sees: Careful at 79, 'What if I can't?', money at 3am, putting off what matters most. This headline confirms the chill self-image he hides behind.
leanings_wrong: Make-up: Quiet mind (83/100). This is his self-image. His friend says he games until 3 or 4 so he does not have to think, which is not a settled mind. Self-report mostly explains it, though his 'I can't settle to anything' answer pointed the other way.
help_card_wrong: "Argue it out with me. Win fairly and I will come round." He dodges every argument, and he comes round to whoever spoke last without being won. Anyone who argues it out with Jake will get 'haha yeah', not his real view.
wording_issues: "Later they remember it, and start looking for ways to get even." This is unfair to Jake, who shows no vengefulness.
"Guard your heart after the win." It is unclear what 'the win' is.

"Gregory says this is the one closest to peace of mind.  One caution from Chrysostom: calm that is never tested is not yet patience. Stay among people." A double space. 'Stay among people' is aimed at someone who is always among people. The real point for him, that his calm is avoidance and not patience, is not drawn.
"Sloth is frequently looked upon as a maintenance of peace" is quoted twice (a link and the counterfeit). The 'pleasure borders on mirth' quote is also used twice.
"How you speak: Full in both. You think things through, and the words come easily." This is identical to p05's. 'Worthy of praise' flatters someone who rarely says what he actually wants.
"Your gladness is a gift. Kept close to God, it becomes the joy Christ promised". This is generic, and it addresses the mask rather than the anxious, unsure young man under it.

"(They picked: gladly do: Sit with them at the hospital, or through a bad night. / Explain something until they finally understand it.; people come for: ...)" This reads like debug output: third person, with '.;' punctuation.

type_why: The Spark was picked on a razor-thin call. Mood came out at 42 (balanced) and Nerve at 50 (dead centre), yet the page tells her flatly "Your mood is light". Everything built on that is off for Grace. She is not a starter who fails to finish. Her trap is not pleasure (the same report says Lust troubles her least), and a young Augustine who loved jokes and pleasure is no kindred to a 45-year-old ward sister. The Forge ("Intense, driven, and cannot stand things done badly... Your anger feels like justice... You wear people out, yourself included. Rest feels like losing") describes her almost line for line: the shoes in the corridor, the sharp corrections, never saying she is tired. The report's own leanings (Lets them know, Fiery, Takes a stand) and its virtue section (Zeal, and temper that calls itself zeal) are Forge material, so the page contradicts itself. It also shares its header, portrait, trap, kindred and first two links word for word with p09, a 31-year-old party-loving salon owner. Biggest miss: her friend's whole verdict is "a saint to strangers and a sergeant to her own family". Grace confessed exactly that when she answered that people she has just met get the best of her. But the Seen-and-unseen scale mixed that answer with "I don't much mind what people think", and it came out at 50. The questions caught the most important thing about her and the report threw it away.

links.link: You said you let people know on the spot. You also said you snap
links.why: Her evening scolding, which bothers her at night. "The care arrives too late" is exactly her pattern with Peter and the children.

links.link: You said you tell people in charge when they are wrong. You also said your anger usually feels justified
links.why: She trusts her own judgement and hates being second-guessed, least of all by her husband. "The feeling of being right is not proof" is what her family needs her to hear.

links.link: You said you hold back after a hard day. You also said you notice when other people overindulge
links.why: It is indirect because it is framed around food and fasting. But the dynamic is hers: she denies herself (five hours of sleep, never admits tiredness, keeps money tight) and then resents the household's slackness. It would land harder pointed at home.

links.link: You said you fix things and move on. You also said you stop doing the wrong thing, but you are not one for saying sorry
links.why: "Something still needs saying" is the apology her family never gets. "Stopping is good" assumes she stops, and she does not: it happens again the next evening. That part is a limit of self-report.

fight_should_be: Pride is right, and her sister's line confirms it: she believes she must carry everything and will not let Peter carry anything. But the description misses that shape of pride. It gives correction-resistance, which fits, and "Thinking every serious talk is aimed at you", which does not fit her at all. Anger scored 44, below Greed (65) and Gluttony (58), which is hard to believe for someone whose strongest leanings are Lets them know, Fiery and Takes a stand.
line_why: Caregiver (the teen mother at 3am, the hospital) and second Giver (funeral collections, fundraisers) are exactly right. The irony her sister sees, that the family gets what is left, is not the line's job to catch.
leanings_wrong: Seen and unseen: balanced (50/100). She answered that people she has just met get the best of her, and her sister's whole verdict is saint to strangers, sergeant at home. The scale mixes 'who gets your best' with 'do you care what people think' and cancels her to the centre. This is the report's biggest single miss, and the questions did catch it.
Mood: balanced (42/100) is honest, but the type text then states 'Your mood is light' as fact.
help_card_wrong: "Ask for my help. I will give it gladly." is true, but it feeds the pattern her sister names: she carries everything. Nothing on the card tells Peter how to get her to hand something over.
wording_issues: "Gregory says many quarrels grow from pride in a gift that sets us apart, like knowing more or trying harder.  Counsel:" The only leaning with no quotation. There is a double space where the quote should be, so the claim is unsourced on the page.
"Last on Cassian's list, and first in its roots." Unclear.
"Full in both." A cryptic label on its own.
"Your strength: Courage. Its partner: Counsel. You act bravely." Reads like a code, not a sentence about her.
"All eight: Pride 100, Greed 65, Gluttony 58..." A numeric score on sins reads as a verdict number against a person.
"(They picked: gladly do: Sit with them at the hospital... ; people come for: ...)" Debug-looking text.
"Kindred: Augustine, as a young man: Before his conversion..." Double colon.
best_moment: "It is not that you do not care. It is that the care arrives too late."
worst_moment: "One more drink, one more episode, one more look than you meant to give." This is said to a Mothers' Union nurse who sleeps five hours and pushes through every dull task. It does not describe her. "One more look" reads as an insinuation about lust, and the same report later says Lust troubles her least. Close second: "How you speak: Full in both... Gregory calls this speaker 'worthy of praise'." She said she sometimes speaks before thinking, and her whole problem is her tongue at home. The praise clashes with the report's own anger section.

type_why: The Lookout is a clear and correct call (Careful 96, Restless 25): he checks the gas, the homework and the email, worries in loops, and cannot nap. "You can mistake fear for wisdom" and the counterfeit "Fear can call itself caution" turn his self-view ("my worrying is just good sense") inside out. Weaker parts: Moses and Gideon are reluctant men who begged off. Daniel is the opposite, an over-responsible man who takes over, so the kindred is generic. "You say yes to too much" also misses. He does not over-commit; he redoes other people's work. What the report cannot see from his answers: that he is "never really in the room", and that his son is starting to fear disappointing him. No question asks about presence, so that is a limit of self-report. But the control his wife names was partly in his answers: he quietly thinks he would do most things better than others (x12), finds it hard to admit someone else's way was better (x7), and usually goes ahead anyway (mi2). The report never joins these, except obliquely in the inner-argument link.

links.link: You said you keep your disagreements with people in charge to yourself
links.why: He is polite to his superiors and fears being passed over. "Some of what feels like humility may be fear of how it will land" fits well.

links.link: You said a friend's success stings a little
links.why: His competitiveness (golf, promotion) is real, but "the sting is a compliment you have not said out loud" is a pleasant reframe that could be said to anyone. It does not reach his fear of falling behind, for himself or for his son.

links.link: You said your gut says "let me think" when a friend asks for money
links.why: "It is not greed for more. It is fear of less." Mortgage, academies, 3am money. It is precise and gentle.

links.link: You said you listen more than you talk. You also said you have whole conversations in your head
links.why: This is the nearest the report gets to what Soo-jin sees: the cold, silent verdicts, and rewriting the team's reports rather than talking to them. "An argument nobody can answer is easy to win" is new information for him.

fight_should_be: Greed as fear of less is well explained and real for him. But the top five are within 12 points (Greed 100, Sadness 92, Listlessness 92, Vainglory 91, Pride 88), so naming one as 'Right now' overstates the certainty. 'Close behind: Sadness' picks arbitrarily between two ties. The friend's word is control, and that is pride in its quiet form: trusting no one's work but his own, which his own x12 answer states. Pride deserves naming alongside greed. The absence his wife describes is nearer listlessness (restless, there and not there) than greed.
line_why: He is the Giver: he pays for things before anyone asks and is generous with his parents. Teacher second fits the homework-checking. Note that the Giver line sits awkwardly next to 'Having: Careful with what you have (83)', and the report does not reconcile them. He is careful for his own household and open-handed to his parents.
leanings_wrong: Pace: Puts it off (75/100). Daniel does not procrastinate. He works late and over-checks. His 'wait until I'm sure' is perfectionism, not putting off. This produces the wrong strength line, 'The risk is that you never get round to doing it.'
Temper: Fiery (25/100). He rarely gets loud and goes cold and precise. 'Fiery' is the wrong word, although the Hard wood section gets the same anger right.
help_card_wrong: "Argue it out with me. Win fairly and I will come round." This is his self-image. His own answers say he rarely changes his mind and usually goes ahead anyway, and his wife says he trusts no one's judgement. Read by Soo-jin, it would sound false.
"Point out everything. I would rather know." It clashes with item 2 ('Start with what I did well') and would feed the never-finished perfectionism the report warns about elsewhere.
wording_issues: "Your strength: Counsel. Its partner: Courage. You think it through well. The risk is that you never get round to doing it." Cryptic, and wrong for him.
"All eight: Greed 100, Sadness 92, Listlessness 92, Vainglory 91, Pride 88..." Five near-maximum numbers against a person read as crushing.
"Close behind: Sadness." Listlessness is tied at 92.
"these think what they do to be exceedingly despised" An archaic quote that needs its paraphrase to be understood.
"Kindred: Moses: When God called him..." Double colon.
best_moment: "And an argument nobody can answer is easy to win. It can leave you quietly judging people who never got to reply."
worst_moment: "Gregory's cure for your kind is to see it coming. Before the day starts, think through what might go wrong and how you will meet it calmly." For a man whose core trouble is looping over what might go wrong, this prescribes more of the thing that keeps him awake. The anger grid's cure is right for an ordinary hard-wood temper and wrong for a Lookout. It should be conditioned on type.

type_why: The Spark is a clear call (Light 13, Restless 17). She fills a room, plays pagode loud and starts a diet every Monday, so 'You start more than you finish' lands. Young Augustine (talk, jokes, friends, pleasure, then conversion) is a fair kindred for a seeker. What the report cannot see: the ten minutes crying on the back step. Her answers said her mood is light, so that is a limit of self-report. What it could have seen and did not: her friend's 'she spends to feel better and to be liked'. She said she cares too much what people think (se2), gives on impulse and regrets it (hv2), wants her good work noticed (x12), and when low wants someone to want her (x5). Together those point at giving to be liked. Yet Vainglory scored 35, and no link joins them.

links.link: You said you let people know on the spot. You also said you snap
links.why: She flares at a rude client, says what she can't take back, and stews a day. It is her pattern exactly (the text is identical to p07's).

links.link: You said you tell people in charge when they are wrong. You also said your anger usually feels justified
links.why: The overcharging supplier and rude clients. 'The feeling of being right is not proof' fits a temper her friend says has cost her good clients.

links.link: You said your mood is usually light. You also said after a hard day you treat yourself
links.why: It repeats the type's trap paragraph with the same quotation, so the quote appears twice in one report. It misses that she also buys when she is sad, and to be liked. And it never says the plain thing, money, even though 'treat yourself' is her spending.

links.link: You said you are nothing but glad when friends succeed
links.why: 'Do not only cheer from the stands' has nothing to grip in her life. She is no spectator: she runs her own salon alone.

fight_should_be: Gluttony is written as food only ('Eating when you are not hungry. Wanting the dish to be different'), and its cure ('break your own fast gladly for a guest') speaks to someone who fasts. Her real comfort-seeking is spending: the new dryer, the dinners, the statements in the drawer. Either the gluttony text should cover reaching for comfort of any kind, or Anger (75) should lead, since her friend says it has driven off good clients. Vainglory at 35 looks under-scored for someone who 'spends to be liked'.
line_why: Caregiver fits the hours at the clinic with her mother. Host second fits the dinners for her girlfriends and the free hair for the neighbour's daughter.
leanings_wrong: Your mind: Holds firm (25/100). She 'loves quickly and trusts too fast', and a man from church is messaging her. Holds firm is her self-view as a fighter, and the simulated answerer flagged the conflict. Partly a limit of self-report, but it matters for what she is weighing.
wording_issues: "Gregory did not soften it: of the four, he calls this the worst. It is also the one where a little work changes the most." The second sentence reads as Gregory's but has no source. It is an unsupported reassurance sitting next to a real quotation.
"The fix is simple: think first." Glib and a little preachy for a temper that is driven by feeling.
"Right now: Gluttony. Not eating well." 'Not eating well' reads as 'poor diet', which is confusing.
"Give steadily and cheerfully, and do not keep score." She is R$18,000 in debt, and keeping score is not her problem. Not looking at the numbers is.
"All eight: Gluttony 100, Anger 75, Pride 67, Lust 57..." Numeric sin scores read as a verdict against the person.
best_moment: "Counterfeit: Giving without thought. Scattering can call itself generosity."
worst_moment: "Eating when you are not hungry. Wanting the dish to be different. A heavy, dull mind afterwards." This is her one 'fight', and it is about food, when the comfort she reaches for is the card. She would shrug it off and miss the point her friend most wants her to hear. Runner-up: 'Quick and lasting... he calls this the worst'. Her stewing is regret over what she said, not held anger, so the label is harsher than her pattern.

type_why: 'Careful' and 'you keep busy' fit a man who gets up at six, bangs around the garage and mows the neighbour's lawn. But the Lookout's 'thinks ahead', 'would rather over-prepare' and 'sees the risks first' is not a man who is putting off the aide, the doctor and the knee, and who 'doesn't think too hard about any of it'. His son calls him the most decent man he knows. He says he needs no fuss and doesn't much mind what people think. That is closer to the Oak ('steady, needs no one's approval'), which the report names as his OPPOSITE. Moses's forty years in the desert suits his long care for June. Gideon's fear does not. What his friend sees (too proud to admit he is drowning, won't ask for help) is only partly visible to self-report. No item asks about accepting help, so the report can't be blamed for missing it directly.

links.link: You said you listen more than you talk
links.why: The same text appears word for word in p12's report. Pairing listening with conversations in the head is sharp. But the payoff, 'quietly judging people who never got to reply', misses Bob. His silence hides his own need, not verdicts on others.

links.link: You said you fix things and move on
links.why: This is a real pair in his answers. The debtor image suits an old-school man who stops doing a thing but won't say sorry. It is a fair small nudge, not an aha.

links.link: You said you are nothing but glad
links.why: Telling a worn-out 78-year-old caregiver not to 'only cheer from the stands' and to try harder is off-target and preachy. 'Gregory's one warning is for people exactly like you' overclaims.

links.link: You said you let rudeness go
links.why: This is templated, identical in p12's report. His real flashpoint is June asking the same question for the fifth time, not rudeness. 'Wishing you had been harsher' is not him, though 'the evening after' loosely touches his blue evenings.

fight_should_be: Pride is the right name, since his son says he is too proud to admit he is drowning. But the report describes it wrongly: 'Thinking every serious talk is aimed at you' is not Bob. His pride shows as refusing help: the aide, the doctor, the video calls. 'Cassian says vainglory feeds it' is odd when his own vainglory score is 20. Sadness (83) belongs beside it as the close second: the lonely evenings, the westerns, the wearing out.
line_why: He picked sitting with someone through a bad night, and he is caring for his wife with Alzheimer's. 'You sit with people, and you do not leave' is exactly him.
help_card_wrong: 'Do not push. I come round in my own time.' and 'Give me a push. I am slow to get going.' are on the same card. His daughter, who wants the aide, gets opposite instructions.

The card never says what his family most needs to know: he will not ask for help. Self-report could not easily catch this, but 'Ask for my help. I will give it gladly' points the wrong way for his situation.
leanings_wrong: 'Say it straight' is shown as a top-three trait, and the report glosses it with Gregory on 'the bold' who need several people to rebuke them. Bob is not bold. His own answer (he5) was that hearing it from one person in private gets through, and the counsel 'Do not wait for a crowd' contradicts it.
'Restless mind' (33) names a racing mind. What the items actually measure is keeping busy. Bob keeps busy so as not to sit with it, and he 'doesn't think too hard about any of it'.
best_moment: "Counterfeit: Delay. Putting off can pass for thinking it through."
worst_moment: "One caution from Chrysostom: calm that is never tested is not yet patience. Stay among people." His calm is tested every hour by June's repeated questions. The report assumes his patience is untried, which would sting a man who is quietly wearing out. Nothing in his answers suggested his calm is untested.
wording_issues: "Gregory says stubbornness often passes for constancy, and grows from thinking a little too much of our own judgment.  Counsel:" has a double space where a quotation is missing.
"(They picked: gladly do: Sit with them at the hospital, or through a bad night. / Quietly pay for something they can’t afford.; people come for: )" is debug residue with an empty field.
"Careful by disposition. Restless by make-up." uses inside-baseball labels.
"Your strength: Counsel. Its partner: Courage." is cryptic, and the same line appears in 15 of 24 reports.
"Gregory’s one warning is for people exactly like you" overclaims.
"How it shows: Finding correction hard to take, even when it is fair. Thinking every serious talk is aimed at you." The second fragment is unsupported for him.

"You think deeply, but the words come hard." contradicts a man who 'doesn't think too hard about any of it'. 'Try writing it down first' does not suit a 78-year-old machinist who won't learn video calls.

type_why: The headline 'The Still Water: Listens first, keeps the peace, and thinks it through' sits directly above 'Strongest leanings: Takes a stand, Fiery, Lets them know'. Her own leanings say Speaks up, Takes a stand (0/100) and Fiery (8/100), and the type paragraph says the opposite ('you would rather listen than talk... keep the peace than win'). She is sharp, argues online at eleven at night and has a remark for everything, so she will mock the headline and distrust the rest. The kindred are inverted too: Gregory the Theologian as the calm, gentle one; Jeremiah too young to speak; silent Arsenius. So is 'Your opposite: The Herald'. 'Careful' is real, since she expects the worst. The trap line says fear 'looks like worry', but for her it looks like realism. Her friend says the cynicism is armour. Her answers (n1, m3, n3) show the pessimism, so the report could have said so. 'You say less than you mean' and 'You carry hurts home' land, but only by accident of the template.

links.link: You said you let people know on the spot
links.why: 'It is not that you do not care. It is that the care arrives too late.' That is the impatient phone call with her mother, followed by three hours with the shopping.

links.link: You said you tell people in charge
links.why: Fair to her remarks about the principal and her online arguing. 'Neither means you are wrong' keeps it from preaching.

links.link: You said things stay with you
links.why: Only partly. This is the closest the report gets to her friend's view that she is more hurt than angry, but it frames it as heaviness feeding anger rather than hurt coming out as cutting. Her answers could have carried it the rest of the way: one raised eyebrow stays all day, a criticism outlasts a compliment, and what someone said keeps her up at 3am.

links.link: You said a friend’s success stings
links.why: A fair reading of two answers with a nice gloss, but nothing in her life points to envy. It takes the slot the hurt pattern needed.

fight_should_be: Anger is the visible fight and her answers support it. 'Going cold on people while saying you are fine' is good. But her friend's view is that she is more hurt than angry, and more tired than she lets on. The truer frame is hurt (Sadness) coming out as anger. Sadness scores only 41 because she answers as a realist. 'What feeds it: Cassian says greed feeds it' is confusing for her, since greed is her LOWEST score (12). She also drinks two or three glasses of wine most nights. Gluttony at 79 is shown only as a number, which is probably wise, but nothing links comfort to the tiredness.
line_why: She picked Teacher and Advocate for both questions. She tears a lazy essay apart and then lends the pupil a life-changing book, and she argues about housing and the Church. Both fit.
help_card_wrong: 'Point out everything. I would rather know.' is her self-image. Her own answers (a criticism stays longer than a compliment; one raised eyebrow stays all day) and her friend ('the softest person in any room') say a full list will wound her.
'Point out everything' and 'Say "next time, try this", not "you did this wrong"' pull in opposite directions, and the card does not say why.
leanings_wrong: The header's 'Listens first, keeps the peace' contradicts her own Talk, Disagreements and Temper results.

'Make-up: Quiet mind (63)', 'Quiet by make-up' and 'Give you quiet and you do your best thinking' misname a woman who reads the news too much, lies awake replaying arguments and answered 'I can't settle to anything'. The items measure liking a free weekend, not a quiet mind.

'Candour: Says it plainly (25)': she is plain about opinions, but her friend says she talks a great deal and says almost nothing about herself. This is a self-report limit, and the report does not hint at it.
'Your strength: Counsel... The risk is that you never get round to doing it' does not fit someone scored Rushes in (33) who decides fast.
best_moment: "It is not that you do not care. It is that the care arrives too late."
worst_moment: "The Still Water: Listens first, keeps the peace, and thinks it through." This is the headline, and it describes the opposite of her own top three leanings. A sharp, argumentative English teacher will laugh at it and stop trusting the rest. Close behind: 'Fluent, not deep.' That will read as an insult to a woman whose pride is seeing through things.
wording_issues: "Fluent, not deep. Words come easily, sometimes before the thought is ready." The category name reads as a put-down, and 'not deep' is wrong for her.
"Gregory says many quarrels grow from pride in a gift that sets us apart, like knowing more or trying harder.  Counsel:" has a double space where a quotation is missing.
"What feeds it: Cassian says greed feeds it. Gregory says envy does." Greed is her lowest score.
"It is also the one where a little work changes the most." This is unattributed but sits among Gregory's words, so it reads as if he said it.
"Before the day starts, think through what might go wrong" is given as a cure to a woman who already 'expects the worst, says so out loud'.
"Your care is a gift. Gregory says the fearful should not stay in fear..." This templated paragraph is odd for her.
"Careful by disposition. Quiet by make-up." uses inside-baseball labels.

type_why: Quiet, listens well, keeps the peace, slow to decide, careful with people: that is Samuel. 'You wait to be sure, and sometimes the moment passes' is the young woman at church. 'You carry hurts home with you' is the roommates. One caveat is a pattern, not an error. All three kindred withdrew from company (Gregory fled ordination, Arsenius fled the world, Jeremiah pleaded he was too young). 'Give you quiet and you do your best thinking' leans into the withdrawal his cousin worries about. The report never says that quiet can become isolation, or that he is lonely, which self-report can't see because he doesn't think he is. His guilt about ever enjoying anything is also missed, though 'Keeps a tight rein (92)' and 'Hard on yourself (83)' were there to link.

links.link: You said you listen more than you talk
links.why: His irritation at his roommates piles up unspoken, so 'quietly judging people who never got to reply' is a fair and useful mirror for him, even though the text is templated.

links.link: You said you let rudeness go
links.why: This is his roommate pattern: calm at the time, then it builds until he leaves for his cousin's for a weekend. The text is templated, shared with p10.

links.link: You said you keep your disagreements
links.why: This is the best link in the report. 'Many are silent through fear, and yet consider that they are silent from humility' hits the gap his cousin sees: he believes he is more patient than he is. It also covers the woman he does not approach.

links.link: You said you hold back after a hard day
links.why: He finds the late-night bar crowd degrading and notices others' mess, so the warning against 'the pride of abstinence' is fair and gently put. But it is the only thing said about his austerity, and his cousin's worry points the other way: he never lets himself enjoy anything.

fight_should_be: Sadness is the right fight. But the description ('The people you love come round, and everything they say seems badly timed'; 'Cassian says anger feeds it') misses what it is for him: loneliness and homesickness, four years from home with no one real here. Cassian's sadness after a loss would have fitted if it had been named plainly. 'Close behind: Greed' (93) is wrong. His thrift is self-denial for the sake of the $600 he sends home each month. If anything comes close behind, it is weariness and a self-denial that allows him no joy.
line_why: The Giver, with the Watcher second. He sends $600 a month home on a rideshare wage and prays. It is right.
help_card_wrong: 'Do not push. I come round in my own time.' is item 1 and 'Give me a push. I am slow to get going.' is item 3. The same card gives opposite instructions.
'Say it gently. A hint is enough.' He also answered 'Tell me plainly what to do'. For someone working in his second language, a hint is the likeliest thing to be missed.
leanings_wrong: 'Having: Careful with what you have (83)' feeds Greed 93 in the private section. His carefulness is sacrifice for his mother and sisters, not holding on for himself. The items ask whether he keeps money back, never for whom, so the questions could reasonably have caught this and did not. It also contradicts the report's own 'The Giver... You serve by giving. Money'.
best_moment: "Some of what feels like humility may be fear of how it will land."
worst_moment: "Close behind: Greed." (Greed 93.) He sends $600 a month home on a rideshare wage, owns two pairs of shoes and feels guilty buying anything for himself. The label reads his sacrifice as avarice, in the same report that calls him The Giver. It would hurt, and it is unfair.
wording_issues: "Close call: your second disposition is close; you could also be The Deep Well." This is jargon, and it says 'close' twice.
"Close call: your make-up is balanced; you could also be The Lookout." uses inside-baseball wording.
"Later they remember it, and start looking for ways to get even." This is harsh and does not fit him. He withdraws to a cousin's; he does not get even.
"How it shows: The people you love come round, and everything they say seems badly timed." This is an odd, unclear sentence for him.
"Your strength: Counsel. Its partner: Courage." is a cryptic, templated line (it appears in 15 of 24 reports).

type_why: Careful fits her exactly (Nerve 100). The trap is the report's best stroke: 'It looks like worry. What if they are upset?' is Chloe. Quiet mind is wrong. She answered that her thoughts get worse when she has nothing to do, she overthinks every chest twinge and every text, and she runs to settle herself. So 'Give you quiet and you do your best thinking' goes against her own answer, and 'Still Water' is the wrong picture for a mind that never stops churning. The Lookout (careful and restless, 'sees the risks first') fits her anxious watchfulness better. The report does flag the Lookout as a close call, which partly saves it. The kindred work: Nazianzen's gentleness and Jeremiah feeling too young to speak both suit her. Arsenius fleeing the world to pray suits her less.

links.link: You said you let rudeness go. You also said hours later...
links.why: This is the dishes. She stays calm, then fumes silently later. 'The hard part for you is not staying calm. It is the evening after' names her pattern. It stops one step short of what her friend sees: after the fuming she feels guilty for minding at all.

links.link: You said a mistake stays with you for a long time. You also said you are quick to say sorry...
links.why: She says sorry forty times a day, to furniture too, as an anxious reflex. She is not repenting of the same sin again and again. Gregory's washed-then-back-in-the-mud warning treats her apologies as sin she keeps repeating, and it tells her the sorrow 'cannot do the work of changing'. Her friend's worry is the opposite: she already thinks she is selfish far more often than she is. The item af2 bundles 'quick to say sorry' with 'do it again anyway', so the question built this error.

links.link: You said you listen more than you talk. You also said you have whole conversations...
links.why: Half true. The silent fuming at her housemates is private judging. But most of her inner talk is rehearsing texts and asking whether SHE offended someone. The accusation turns on herself, not on others. The quote about the silent exalting their mind leans on pride, which is her lowest of the eight (12).

links.link: You said you keep your disagreements with people in charge to yourself...
links.why: She answered 'It's not my place.' Reading that as fear dressed as humility names exactly why she can't tell a doctor he is wrong. It also backs her friend's view that she is stronger than she thinks. This is a real aha.

anger_why: Slow to light and burning where nobody sees fits the silent fuming. 'Once it is lit, it stays lit' goes beyond the evidence: her fuming turns into guilt, not a grudge. The cure prescribed ('Before the day starts, think through what might go wrong') is what an anxious overthinker already does too much.
speaker_why: 'Deep, but held in' fits her with anyone in authority. She is fluent and funny with friends once relaxed, so the label is only half her. 'Try writing it down first' is odd advice for someone who rewrites every text five times.
fight_should_be: Sadness. Six months ago her friend was killed. She reads Luke in bed at night and wonders if what she feels is real. She came out heavy-hearted (75) and 'dwells on a mistake' (0), and the report itself ranks sadness second (70) and names it as what feeds her listlessness. Listlessness's picture (watching the clock, drifting, wanting to be anywhere else) does not fit a woman who works 20+ hours around nursing placements and takes every extra shift. It won mostly on x11, where the other side ('I like people to know what I've done') was so unlike her that she pushed hard to A, and on a pace score that measures indecision, not idleness.
line_why: A nursing student who is gentle with patients and good at noticing when someone is scared, and who hears things people tell no one else. 'You sit with people, and you do not leave' is her. The only gap is that the listener role has no line of its own.
virtue_why: Peace, with avoidance as its counterfeit, is exactly the doormat problem her friend names. But the quote's word 'sloth' is the wrong word for someone this overworked.
help_card_wrong: Items 4 and 6 say the same thing twice: 'Start with what I did well.' and 'Tell me what I did well. It makes me try harder.'
leanings_wrong: Seen and unseen: 'Better in public (17/100)'. Gregory's pair is about good in public and bad in secret. Chloe does her good unseen: she reads Luke telling nobody and washes other people's dishes. Her 'care what people think' is people-pleasing anxiety, not a public face. The label hints at a hypocrisy she doesn't have, and it fed her Vainglory score. She herself flagged item se1 as ambiguous.
Make-up: 'balanced (58)', read as quiet. Her idle thoughts get worse and she runs to settle them. This pushed her into Still Water rather than the Lookout.

Pace: 'Puts it off (92)'. It fairly catches her indecision ('whatever you're having', the Christmas choice). As a label it reads as procrastination for someone who never turns down a shift, and it helped crown Listlessness.
wording_issues: 'Guard your heart after the win.' What win? Gregory's 'victory' over impatience will not come through to a reader.
'Close call: your make-up is balanced; you could also be The Lookout.' 'Make-up' reads as cosmetics. It is jargon.
'Break outward peace with him, but guard in your heart's core internal peace concerning him' is archaic and hard to parse on a phone.
'Later they remember it, and start looking for ways to get even.' This is too harsh for someone whose after-anger is guilt, not revenge.
'Your strength: Counsel. Its partner: Courage. You think it through well. The risk is that you never get round to doing it.' Word for word the same in all three reports I judged.
'(They picked: gladly do: Sit with them at the hospital, or through a bad night. / Have them over and cook them a meal.; people come for: ...)' reads like debug output with stacked colons.
'Before the day starts, think through what might go wrong and how you will meet it calmly.' This advice feeds her anxiety.
best_moment: "Some of what feels like humility may be fear of how it will land."
worst_moment: "Gregory describes people who wash, and then walk straight back into the mud. Feeling bad is real, but it cannot do the work of changing." She says sorry forty times a day as a nervous reflex and already thinks she is selfish far more than she is. This reads her apologies as repeated sin and feeds the false guilt her friend worries about. For a grieving seeker it could also be the line that makes the whole thing feel like a scolding.
misses_friend_view: It catches the doormat (lets it go, keeps the peace, makes yourself small, open-handed) and hints at hidden strength ('love does what fear used to do'). It never says what Priyanka says: that she is much stronger than she thinks, and that minding is not selfish. The mud link pushes the other way. Her grief and her secret faith are out of reach of a self-report, except through sadness, which the report ranked second.

type_why: Serious by disposition is right, and it gently corrects his self-image ('not gloomy, only realistic'). Restless is honest to his answers: busyness keeps the dread away. But the Forge copy paints an open crusader: 'you move fast', 'driven', 'People know where they stand with you', with Chrysostom and Jerome as fighters who argue in public. Viktor is braced and closed. His wife calls him a closed door the war bolted. He goes silent, not polemical, and he sits in his car for half an hour. The Deep Well ('grave, feels things all the way down') is closer to what Halyna sees, though his answers did not choose it. The trap ('being right about how badly you have been treated') also misses a man who never complains about his own pain.

links.link: You said you listen more than you talk. You also said you have whole conversations in your head...
links.why: This is his stubborn verdict that a person 'isn't serious', reached in his head and never argued out. 'An argument nobody can answer is easy to win' fits him better than it fits most.

links.link: You said you fix things and move on. You also said you stop doing the wrong thing, but you are not one for saying sorry...
links.why: He quit drinking alone and told nobody. 'Stopping is good... Something still needs saying' points straight at the unspoken debt to Halyna for the drinking years. The report could not know about the drinking, and it still lands. The strongest line in the three reports.

links.link: You said things stay with you for a while. You also said once you are angry, it can last for days...
links.why: No message from Andriy means gruff and silent until evening. A heavy heart sliding into anger is exactly that, and it challenges his 'only realistic' self-image fairly.

links.link: You said you are careful about small things. You also said your worst mistakes are rare, but big...
links.why: Plausible for a careful mechanic whose big fall was drink, but it lands on nothing in particular. Gnat-and-camel is Christ's charge of hypocrisy, which is heavy for a careful workman.

anger_why: Lasting fits: he is gruff until evening. But what lasts is mostly dread for his son, and the report reads it as temper. The first cure ('think through what might go wrong, so nothing catches you asleep') is what he already does every morning. He expects bad news and braces for it.
speaker_why: 'Deep, but held in' is the closed door. 'Saying it to one person' is exactly the talk Halyna wants.
fight_should_be: Sadness (83, a close second). Pride has real evidence: the stubborn verdicts, not trying to learn Polish, 'sure of your work', and answers x7, x9 and x12. His friend's picture is Cassian's dejection, though: fear for a son moved closer to the front, the half hour in the car, the gruff silence until a message comes, carrying everything alone. The Pride page also misfires in detail. 'Thinking every serious talk is aimed at you' matches nothing in him. Its named feeder, vainglory, is one of his lowest scores (37), and he wants no attention at all.
line_why: 'You notice what people need and you meet it' is the free car repair and the money refused three times, 'kinder than his face'. The line frames giving as money, though ('Quietly pay...', 'give alms'). His giving is his hands and his skill. And the same report calls him 'Careful with what you have'.
virtue_why: Diligence fits the mechanic. The counterfeit, 'Restlessness of spirit is frequently termed a watchful solicitude', could have been a bullseye (checking the phone for Andriy before anything else), but the report never makes that link. 'Not being able to stop' misses a man who sits still in his car.
help_card_wrong: 'Give me a push. I am slow to get going.' He wakes before the alarm and does what needs doing. It also sits on the same card as 'Do not push. I come round in my own time.'
leanings_wrong: Having: 'Careful with what you have (67)'. He refused money three times for a free repair, and the report makes him The Giver. The caution is a refugee's thin wallet, not his character.

Disagreements: 'Takes a stand (8)'. His stubbornness is real but silent. He doesn't argue things out. He can't bring himself to have the one talk his wife is asking for. 'Takes a stand' pictures an open arguer.
wording_issues: 'Gregory says stubbornness often passes for constancy, and grows from thinking a little too much of our own judgment.  Counsel:'. There is a double space where a quotation should be. Render gap.
'Gregory says many quarrels grow from pride in a gift that sets us apart, like knowing more or trying harder.  Counsel:'. The same missing quote.
'Pride spoils them all.  How it shows:'. The same missing quote.
'You get done what others only talk about.' (type) against 'The risk is that you never get round to doing it.' (strength). The report contradicts itself.
'Do not push. I come round in my own time.' and 'Give me a push. I am slow to get going.' are both on one card.
'Kindred: St John Chrysostom: A friend from his youth called him irritable, and an admiring historian says it was his nature to rebuke wrongdoing.' Colons and clauses stacked.
'Thinking every serious talk is aimed at you.' Unclear what a 'serious talk' is here.
'What feeds it: Cassian says vainglory feeds it.' His vainglory is 37.
best_moment: "Stopping is good. But Gregory says it does not undo what was done, any more than a debtor clears a debt by borrowing no more. Something still needs saying."
worst_moment: "People know where they stand with you." His wife's whole view is that he is a closed door the war bolted. The type paints a fast, driven crusader with fighter saints for kindred, over a man who goes silent and sits in his car. And it never names the fear for his son that sits under the gruffness.
misses_friend_view: 'Keeps it in', 'Deep, but held in' and the saying-sorry link catch the closed door. The Giver line catches 'kinder than his face'. What it misses is the grief and fear. Self-report could partly catch that (sadness came out 83) but the report steers it into anger and pride.

type_why: Cheerful and quiet is Priya. 'Easy to be around', 'an evening at home' and 'People relax when you walk in' match Anu's 'easy to be with' and her hour with a Malayalam film. But mostly it confirms her self-view pleasantly. The misfire is the type's trap and cost copy: 'One more drink... one more look', 'Pleasure can quietly become the point'. Nothing in her life shows that. She is a dutiful Mar Thoma mother whose treats are a film and one sari at Onam.

links.link: You said you let things slide that you probably should not. You also said you calm things down...
links.why: This is Anu's point about going along with the in-laws to keep the peace, which she has not put into words herself. 'Keeping the peace can be love. It can also be the easier road' is fair and useful. The quote's word 'sloth' is harsh for a working mother.

links.link: You said your mood is usually light. You also said after a hard day you treat yourself...
links.why: It calls pleasure 'the one pull you are least guarded against', and the quote holds out lust as the bait. Her own fight page ranks lust last of eight (12). She splurges once a year, feels a bit guilty, and gets over it. A light mood plus 'treat yourself' does not show she is unguarded.

links.link: You said you are nothing but glad when friends succeed. You also said you admire lots of people...
links.why: 'Eager backers, but inert spectators' could be said to almost anyone content. She is dependable and kind in practice, not inert. It might brush the promotion question, but it can also read as a push against a healthy contentment.

links.link: You said more of your regrets are things you never got round to. You also said before something big you think about what could go wrong...
links.why: It rests on two slight leans (+1 each) and states 'Those are one habit.' She is 'neither a worrier nor carefree'. She worries, gets busy and forgets. The sluggard who would not plough is the wrong image for a woman running a household and a test team.

anger_why: Kindled reeds is her weekly flare at Joel over the dishes, made up by morning, and her snappy Mondays. 'The danger is the first minute' is accurate and useful.
speaker_why: 'Full in both' rests on a borderline score. On sp2 she actually said she sometimes speaks before thinking it through, so 'You think things through' goes against her own answer. The praise ('worthy of praise') flatters more than it tells.
fight_should_be: No thought clearly leads for her. The head-to-heads crowned whichever lesser evil she picked. If one must lead, Anger has the most evidence in her life (the weekly flare, snappy Mondays), and the report should say her fight is spread thin rather than name Greed. Greed's picture ('It is never quite enough') does not fit a woman who saves a little and splurges on a sari without much guilt. Her worry about 'old age and illness' is about her parents' health, not avarice. Its feeder ('a heart with no joy inside') contradicts the cheerful Hearth the same report makes her.
line_why: She picked Host and it is a fair stand-in. Anu sees her as the sensible one friends go to for level-headed advice. No line offers counsel, and she had to pick Teacher to reach it.
virtue_why: Peace, with avoidance as its counterfeit, is the in-laws point again. But it repeats the same 'Sloth is frequently looked upon as a maintenance of peace' quote already used in link 1.
help_card_wrong: 'Give me a push. I am slow to get going.' Starting is not her trouble. She starts every January, and her strongest leaning is 'Hard to finish'.
'Argue it out with me. Win fairly and I will come round.' Mild: she won't fight about anything twice, and she goes along to keep the peace.
leanings_wrong: Your own work: 'Sure of your work (25/100)'. This moderate lean is headlined as a strongest leaning. Its counsel says the confident 'bristle when corrected', but she takes correction at work without fuss. For a balanced person the top three are weak and should not carry pride warnings.
Room: 'Takes up room (33)'. Her friend says she is too quick to go along with her in-laws, and she won't fight twice. It also sits oddly beside 'Keeps the peace (75)' and 'Easily swayed (67)'.
wording_issues: 'One more drink, one more episode, one more look than you meant to give.' A three-item list tic. It contradicts 'Troubles you least: Lust.' on the same report.

The trap quote 'For because pleasure borders on mirth, he holds out lust as a bait to cheerful dispositions.' appears twice (in the trap and in link 2). 'Sloth is frequently looked upon as a maintenance of peace' also appears twice (in link 1 and the counterfeit).
'What feeds it: Gregory says sadness runs down into it: a heart with no joy inside looks for comfort in owning things.' Stacked colons. It also contradicts her light mood.
'It is a very blameless thing, that thou desirest some things to possess; because thou seekest not to be increased, but art afraid of being in want' is long and archaic for a phone.
'Cassian names Abraham and Lot, and in his own day Macarius, who ran a guest house in Alexandria and was known as "a man of singular courtesy and patience".' Comma-stacked.
'Finish one thing before you start the next.' Her pattern is one routine fading by midyear, not juggling many.
'Gregory's one warning is for people exactly like you' overclaims.
best_moment: "Keeping the peace can be love. It can also be the easier road."
worst_moment: "One more drink, one more episode, one more look than you meant to give." The same report ranks lust last of her eight. Said to a Mar Thoma working mother whose treats are a film and one sari a year, it is unfounded and suggestive, and it could offend.
misses_friend_view: It gets 'easy to be with' and, through the peace links, the in-laws. It barely touches 'the most sensible one'. The trap and fight pages then invent a pleasure problem and a greed problem that neither she nor her friend sees.

type_why: The Spark is Luis on sight: loud, warm, always moving, cannot sit through a meal, laughs things off. 'Quiet feels like a threat, so you fill it' and 'You bounce back fast' (the cold Coke ten minutes after the banged pot) are right. Two misfits. 'You start more than you finish' sits badly on a man who took a taco stand to two restaurants. The kindred Augustine who loved 'reading together and friendly arguments' does not suit a man who has never read a contract through. That line comes with the type template; nothing ties it to him.

links.link: You said you let people know on the spot. You also said you snap
links.why: This is the pot-banging on a Saturday and the Coke ten minutes later. 'The care arrives too late' is exact, and he would recognise it at once.

links.link: You said your mood is usually light. You also said after a hard day you treat yourself
links.why: It is his friend's 'eating himself to death and laughing it off': cheerfulness is what leaves him unguarded. Two weaknesses. It repeats the trap paragraph and its quotation almost word for word. The quotation names lust when his pull is food.

links.link: You said you tell people in charge when they are wrong. You also said your anger usually feels justified
links.why: 'The feeling of being right is not proof' fits the man who says the doctor exaggerates and who distrusts his son's ideas. It reaches the pride under his stubbornness.

links.link: You said you are nothing but glad when friends succeed. You also said you admire lots of people
links.why: It tells a man who built a business from nothing at 22 not to 'only cheer from the stands' and to 'admire it enough to try it'. Gregory's 'inert spectators' is the last thing Luis is. It comes from two mild answers and misreads him.

fight_should_be: Gluttony is right. It is the friend's first worry, and 'God has created all things clean, in order to be eaten' is exactly his joking excuse. Pride scored 94, a near tie, and it is the root of his diabetes denial and his distrust of his son. It could have been named as close behind, as it was for p17 at 97.
line_why: The Host first, the Giver second: the priest who eats free on Thursdays, the stranger's paid lunch, the party he always overpays for. Macarius's guest house in Alexandria is a real reference in Cassian's Conference 14.
best_moment: "Not being able to stop can feel like faithfulness."
worst_moment: "7. Do not push. I come round in my own time." He has ignored his glucose readings for three years, and his doctor is now talking about insulin and nerve damage. On a card meant to be handed to the people around him, this tells his wife and doctor to back off the one thing that is killing him. It sides with his denial.
help_card_wrong: "Do not push. I come round in my own time." His friend and his wife would say the opposite. He has not come round on the diabetes in three years.
leanings_wrong: Seen and unseen: balanced (50/100). His friend says 'His kids miss him'. Regulars, delivery men and strangers get the hugs, and home gets his absence. 'Better in public' fits the friend's view. This is partly a self-report limit, because he answered the one direct item only mildly. Still, the report never mentions his family at all.

Little things: balanced (58/100). He has never read a contract all the way through and he ignores his glucose readings, so 'Easy on little things' fits better. He himself answered 'let small things slide' fairly strongly.
