wording_issues: "(They picked: gladly do: Have them over and cook them a meal. / Quietly pay for something they can’t afford.; people come for: A place to stay, or a meal. / Money, or something they need.)" reads like debug output.
"Gregory says stubbornness often passes for constancy, and grows from thinking a little too much of our own judgment.  Counsel:" has a double space where a quotation was dropped.
"What feeds it: It comes first on Cassian’s list, and it opens the door to the others." does not answer what feeds it.
"Of the four kinds of speaker, Gregory blames only this one": the four kinds are never explained.
"All eight: Gluttony 100, Pride 94, Vainglory 47..." puts scores out of 100 on a person's sins, which reads like the percentage-against-a-person the site forbids.

type_why: The Deep Well fits: serious, quiet, notices what is wrong (the misused word, the recycling). 'Heaviness can become your home' and 'Joy can feel suspicious' quietly touch what Ingrid sees. One line is wrong for her: 'People come to you when something really matters.' When her friend died she had no one to tell. People do not come to her, and that is the heart of what her friend worries about.

links.link: You said you listen more than you talk. You also said you have whole conversations in your head
links.why: This is the aha. She believes she is tolerant, yet inside she runs arguments against her sister, her sister's husband and the grandchildren's names. 'An argument nobody can answer is easy to win' answers her self-image the way Ingrid would.

links.link: You said your gut says “let me think” when a friend asks for money
links.why: 'It is not greed for more. It is fear of less' is kind and exact for a woman facing a hip operation who dreads needing help. Cassian's avarice passage really does name fear of an enfeebled old age. It stays about money. It could have reached the way she holds people off in case they let her down.

links.link: You said you hold back after a hard day. You also said you notice when other people overindulge
links.why: She reports the neighbour's recycling and has an opinion on what everything should cost. 'Judging the undisciplined is where it turns' fits. It overlaps the first link, since both are about quiet judging.

links.link: You said you fix things and move on. You also said you stop doing the wrong thing, but you are not one for saying sorry
links.why: The debtor image, 'Something still needs saying', lands on her sister just before six weeks under one roof. The evidence is her own answer, but it fits her reserve.

fight_should_be: Sadness, which scored 97 against Anger's 100, is almost a tie and it is what her friend actually sees. She is lonelier than she knows, she calls her long silent Sundays peace, and she found she had no one to tell. Cassian says dejection will not let a soul be 'quiet and gentle with the brethren' and makes it 'rough, impatient, hard'. That explains her sharpness at its root instead of treating it as the root. He also says perfection 'is not secured by separating from men'. The Anger card does catch 'Going cold on people while saying you are fine' and 'Irritation at things that cannot help it' (the grandchildren's names). But its 'What feeds it: greed... envy' does not fit her. The questions caught the sadness, so this is the report's choice, not a self-report limit. The report never says the word lonely.
line_why: Teacher suits a retired librarian who explains things. Caregiver second catches the soup for the old man downstairs and the neighbour's cat. Ingrid's 'more generous than anyone sees' shows only here.
best_moment: "And an argument nobody can answer is easy to win. It can leave you quietly judging people who never got to reply."
worst_moment: "Give something away this week that you might have kept." Her friend says she is more generous than anyone sees: soup for the old man, feeding the neighbour's cat, embarrassed to be thanked. The report comes back to tightness three times: the leaning's counsel, the second link, and the counterfeit 'Holding on... niggardliness'. That pile-up is the one read Ingrid would call unfair. Her real holding back is of people, not money.
help_card_wrong: "4. Point out everything. I would rather know." sits oddly beside "7. Say 'next time, try this', not 'you did this wrong'." The two pull against each other on one card. The rest suits her: 'Give me a push' and 'Ask what I think. I rarely offer it' are what got her into the reading circle.
leanings_wrong: Temper: Fiery (25/100). She is cold and exacting, not hot, and by her own answers slow to anger. The report's own anger card says 'It takes a lot to make you angry', so the report contradicts itself. The label comes from 'feel the heat rise at unfairness'. That item measures indignation, and 'Fiery' will read as wrong to her.
wording_issues: "Close call: your second disposition is close; you could also be The Still Water." uses 'close' twice and the jargon word 'disposition'.
"What feeds it: Cassian says greed feeds it. Gregory says envy does." gives two answers, and neither is tied to her.
The money point is made three times in nearly the same words: "Holding on can call itself thrift", "It is not greed for more", "Tightness can call itself good sense".

"Held under reason, the fire in it becomes holy zeal." is aimed at anger. It does not touch her real faith question, whether being moved by Bach counts. No item could catch that, but 'holy zeal' reads as generic for a quiet, unsure Lutheran.

type_why: The Spark matches the Andre on the microphone: lights up a room, hates a pause, restless. But his cheer is partly a mask. When he loses big he is extra cheerful at church, and in private he is very hard on himself and feels like a fraud. The template text takes the cheer at face value. 'You bounce back fast' contradicts his own leaning (Dwells on a mistake, 17/100) and the report's second link. His two top leanings, Chooses what to show and Better in public, see the double life. The type text does not.

links.link: You said you keep your disagreements with people in charge to yourself
links.why: 'Some of what feels like humility may be fear of how it will land' answers his self-image, 'humble, just a vessel', directly. It also bears on the thing he cannot bring himself to tell Brianna. The quotation is a real Moralia line.

links.link: You said a mistake stays with you for a long time. You also said you are quick to say sorry
links.why: This is the betting cycle: remorse, promise, back again, 'I'll stop after the wedding'. 'Feeling bad is real, but it cannot do the work of changing' would land hard. Gregory's washed sow is real, Pastoral Rule III.30. It is the only link printed without its quotation, and it ends on a stray space.

links.link: You said your mood is usually light. You also said after a hard day you treat yourself
links.why: It is a word-for-word copy of the link Luis got. Its quotation is about lust, which Andre scored low on and which is not his pull. 'It looks like a good time' does fit how the betting began, as fun with friends, but the link never gets near that.

links.link: You said a friend’s success stings a little
links.why: The reframe of envy as a compliment is real Gregory and nicely put. But nothing in how his friend sees him points to envy. It comes from two mild answers and misses the need to be 'the guy with the answers'.

fight_should_be: Greed, in Cassian's sense, fits better. Cassian's avarice starts with 'almost reasonable excuses' over a small sum, schemes 'how he can double it', works in secret 'without the Abbot knowing anything about it', and ends in lying and broken promises. That is chasing losses and the second credit card Brianna has never seen. Andre gave the strongest possible answer that money keeps him awake at 3am, yet Greed scored 39 because he is open-handed. Money never appears anywhere in the report. Listlessness catches only a symptom, the phone checked in staff meetings. Vainglory (62), his need to be the guy with the answers who never admits a struggle, would also fit better than Listlessness.
line_why: Teacher, then Shepherd: he preaches to eighty teenagers, remembers every kid's name and their little brother's, and answers texts at midnight.
best_moment: "Some of what feels like humility may be fear of how it will land."
worst_moment: "Your strength: Courage. Its partner: Counsel. You act bravely." It praises courage in a man whose whole crisis is not finding the courage to tell his fiancée, and who is quick to counsel and slow to take it. It also contradicts the report's own best line, that his humility may be fear. It is the Spark template, copied word for word from Luis's report.
help_card_wrong: "3. Tell me what I did well. It makes me try harder." and "7. Start with what I did well." are near duplicates.

The card is all affirmation and pacing. His friend's one instruction would be to ask him straight how he is really doing, because he never admits he is struggling. 'Tell me in private' is the only item that points that way.
leanings_wrong: Room: balanced (42/100). He lights up a room and knows it, and his friend calls him a performer who needs to be the guy with the answers, so 'Takes up room' fits. His self-image of 'just a vessel' pulled it to the middle, which is a self-report limit worth knowing.
wording_issues: "The sorrow is meant to lead somewhere. " is the only link with no quotation and a trailing space, so it looks broken.

"Gregory says this is the one closest to peace of mind.  One caution from Chrysostom: calm that is never tested is not yet patience. Stay among people." has a double space. Chrysostom's caution (On the Priesthood) is about solitaries, and 'Stay among people' is odd advice to a youth pastor who is never alone. It also calls his anger 'closest to peace of mind' when he is curt with volunteers who do not do things his way.
"You bounce back fast" (type) contradicts "a mistake stays with you for a long time" (link 2) in the same report.

"Your gladness is a gift." is the same Christ section Luis got. It misses what his faith line says: he preaches grace well and cannot take it for himself. His answers ('Hard on yourself', 'Dwells on a mistake') gave the report enough to say so.

type_why: The trap fits her inner life: 'being right about how badly you have been treated' is her resentment of the ex, the brother and the old man, which she is ashamed of. The outward portrait is wrong. 'People know where they stand with you', 'you move fast' and 'You tell the truth when it is needed' describe a public fighter, and so do the kindred, Chrysostom and Jerome. She answers mildly, keeps her words few, never says no and swallows everything. Her own top leanings contradict the type: Lets it go 92, Makes yourself small 92, Chooses what to show 75, Keeps it in 67. The close call, The Lookout, fits far better. Its line 'You say yes to too much, afraid of letting people down' is exactly her friend's view, but the report only names it and never explains it.

links.link: You said you let rudeness go. You also said hours later
links.why: This is her: she answers the old man mildly, then scrubs the kitchen very hard. 'The hard part for you is not staying calm. It is the evening after' puts into words something she has not said. It also touches her friend's fear that she will one day explode.

links.link: You said you hold back after a hard day. You also said you notice when other people overindulge
links.why: Her going without is necessity and love: cheap bread and one coat for six years so the house gets built. It is not ascetic discipline. Warning her about 'the pride of abstinence' and 'judging the undisciplined' scolds her for something nothing in her life shows.

links.link: You said things stay with you for a while. You also said once you are angry
links.why: Heaviness feeding a slow grudge fits her resentments. Caveat: she thinks she is more bitter than she is. This link, the anger section ('the worst') and the type all build on that harsh self-image and never soften it.

links.link: You said your gut says “let me think” when a friend asks for money
links.why: 'Fear of less' is a real feeling for her, and the report says so kindly. But it files a divorced carer's saving for her daughter's house under the roots of grasping. It then escalates to Greed 100 in the private section. No question asks who the money is for, so thrift for others scores as avarice. That is a flaw in the questions, not in her.

fight_should_be: Anger, the swallowed kind: resentment she holds in until, as her friend fears, she explodes or falls ill. The report's own link 3 and anger section already point there (Anger 76), and Sadness (74, the separation from Daria) is close behind. Greed misreads her. 'A heart with no joy inside looks for comfort in owning things' and 'Be content with what you need' are said to a woman who owns almost nothing and spends nothing on herself.
line_why: The Caregiver is literally her life. 'You sit with people, and you do not leave' is accurate, though it tells her nothing she did not know. The second line, The Watcher, fits her evening prayers and the icon she kisses.
best_moment: The hard part for you is not staying calm. It is the evening after.
worst_moment: "Give something away this week that you might have kept." She sends nearly every wage home for bricks and windows and has worn one coat for six years. Coming beside a private fight of Greed at 100, this reads as a scold of her sacrifice.
help_card_wrong: 5. Slow me down. I run ahead. The gloss 'I run ahead' has no support in her life and contradicts her own Follow-through leaning (Hard to start). If anything she needs slowing down because she overworks, which is a different point.
leanings_wrong: Follow-through: Hard to start (33/100). Her friend calls her the hardest-working person alive. Her regret over 'things I never got round to' is circumstance (a life on hold abroad), not a temperament that struggles to start.
wording_issues: "Guard your heart after the win." It is unclear what 'the win' is.
"Gregory says grasping grows from two roots, pride and fear, and yours looks like fear." A comma stack.

"Your strength: Counsel. Its partner: Courage. You think it through well. The risk is that you never get round to doing it." This is identical in all three reports and false for her: she does everything.
"Where the trap is set for you: a quarrel." It is odd for someone who avoids every quarrel.
"Your seriousness is not a flaw to be fixed. Held under reason, the fire in it becomes holy zeal." 'Holy zeal' is the Forge template and misses her. She is a patient, prayerful Orthodox mother.
"(They picked: gladly do: Sit with them at the hospital... ; people come for: ...)" This reads like debug output left in the report.
The anger cure "when someone wrongs you, remember your own faults" risks feeding the shame she already feels about her resentment.

type_why: 'Warm, steady, and glad to be where you are' matches her friend's 'fun, steady'. Keeps the peace and Enjoys comforts fit (Friday wine, Cuba in February). The portrait is generic, though ('People relax when you walk in', 'trouble rarely finds you'). It misses the organiser who is always slightly overbooked and short with everyone in tired weeks. The Shepherd line partly rescues this. Antony, twenty years alone in the desert, is a stretch as a kindred for the glue of a hockey-parent group.
